title: I Posted the Shelter Dog-Walk Slot After They Took My Tagged Leash

parts.text: I signed walk slot 3 at 9:14 a.m. and volunteer lead Chris was already out with my tagged leash on a different dog. The whiteboard said: TAG THE LEASH. SLOT IS THE DOG. NO SWAPS. I was thirty-five, walker, holding a slot sticker. Chris shrugged. "Leads are the pack." I photographed the empty hook, the sticker, and his outbound still. Then I logged a swap. At 9:21 the shelter manager asked why Chris's walk was on my tagged leash. I did not argue the joke. I argued the file. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The shelter manager can see Chris outbound on my tagged leash against the slot sticker.

social.video_title: He walked out with my tagged leash on another dog — Part 1/2
social.description: Animal shelter, a slot sticker, and a lead on my leash. I logged the swap. Would you have photographed the hook?

parts.text: Chris called it enrichment until the manager asked for the log. I printed the swap, the photo, and the board. The leash came back. Chris tagged his own and told walkers enrichment was always about optics. Optics is a word leads use when a tag exists. Walk policy now has a second line: LEADS ARE NOT THE PACK. I keep slot 3. Chris signs a different dog. The yard finally looks like a schedule, not a grab. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point. If it is written, it can be applied to the person who wrote it.

social.video_title: Leads are not the pack — Part 2/2
social.description: Swap log, returned leash, and a second line. Was enrichment ever my tag?
